correctness.rationale: Exact Friedlander-Kirchhoff determinant plus weighted matrix-tree theorem gives Q=mean(x)*sum_T product_{e not in T}x_e for connected positive Kirchhoff metric graphs. Monotonicity under increasing lengths and adding an edge of maximal length proves universal K_n extremality with one actual shortest edge; Cayley and edge transitivity give the stated polynomial. Its strict increase yields a unique root and the half-integer boundary, and slightly longer complete-graph edges prove sharpness. n=2 is excluded from the finite-radius formula. The packaged exact verifier checks finite identities, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The source arXiv:2209.01284v2 proves a much smaller sufficient radius, although its determinant formula is an admitted ingredient. The closest follow-up arXiv:2406.17965v3 computes single-edge first-order expansions for selected families and only expects an n^{-n} window (Section 5.3); it neither proves sharp universal simultaneous-edge control nor provides a fixed-topology optimum. Targeted published-published-finding corpus and web searches for aliases, cotree polynomials, sharp radii and complete-graph extremizers did not find an implication-equivalent theorem. This is not a proof that unpublished or weakly indexed equivalent work does not exist.
residual_risks: Potential weakly indexed equivalent sharp-radius theorem phrased in matroid or cotree language.

Earlier determinant identity is sufficiently general to furnish the formula used here; the originality is only the proved optimal extremal threshold and its topology-dependent refinement, not that determinant identity.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 theorem itself says its length window is suboptimal, while its 2025 follow-up explicitly conjectures the larger ell*n^-n scale. This theorem provides an exact, optimal all-topology perturbation cutoff for simultaneously varying all edges, a complete-graph worst case with a genuine shortest-edge normalization, a full asymptotic law and a topology-specific improvement determined by spanning-tree edge-inclusion probabilities. A sharp universal structural cutoff is motivated and mathematically useful even though its derivation uses known determinant identities.
